scope: Targeted Java/PostgreSQL staging, one-shot Flyway and entitlement boundaries before container execution

history.cause: Flyway 12.4.0 treats logger name none as a class name; schema tests and subsequent staging context failed before their assertions.
history.correction: Use supported slf4j logger; container standalone tasks retain dedicated logback OFF configuration.

verified: Fresh Flyway V001-V019, replay with zero additional migrations and no account/order/session/import seed.
Concurrent V018 to V019 upgrade applies the migration once and preserves the existing synthetic account row.
Application role is distinct and restricted; schema/database CREATE privilege is refused while DML and read-only Flyway history are granted.
Staging Spring context starts with Flyway disabled and Hibernate validate after the separate migration.
Staging HTTP health is minimal and private no-store; CSRF creates Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Lax Path=/ session cookie and missing-CSRF logout remains403.
Staging and production require HTTPS public origin plus secure cookies; exactly one matching runtime profile.
Staging ignores MANUAL_TEST access origins; Stripe TEST official endpoint is allowed but LIVE/loopback overrides rejected; production payments remain closed.
unexecutedHere: Container image build, Java HealthProbe execution and non-root/read-only filesystem behavior are not established by this Maven target.
ObjectSnapshotMain compiled with the real AWS SDK, but object export/restore/tamper/non-empty-target integration is delegated to the isolated P20 Docker harness.
The HTTP staging test addresses Spring on loopback and inspects secure cookie headers; actual TLS is delegated to the Caddy image recipe.
The PostgreSQL target uses Testcontainers isolated credentials; a non-superuser migration owner is tested separately by the production Compose recipe.
No complete global API suite was repeated for this narrow configuration/container delta.
